request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollup audit lines are in place, and all 4 acceptance scenarios pass under `bin/e2e`.

**What it does:** the server now measures every person's claimed and due-total, plus the sheet's two totals, just before and just after each change. Changing a rate, adding or editing a person, adding or editing a claim, opening, settling or voiding a claim, taking a statement, and changing the sheet's today are all covered. After the change's own audit line it writes:
- one `ROLLUP` line for each person whose figures moved, in the order people were added. A newly added person always gets one.
- a `TOTALS` line, only if the sheet's claimed-total or due-total moved.

A change that moves no figure writes nothing extra, and changing the sheet's today writes only these lines, with none of its own. All lines are written only once the change is saved, so a refused change still writes nothing.

**Line format:** the spec expects `person=<name>` rather than the `name=<name>` in the request text, and it puts `sheet=`/`by=` first as AGENTS.md requires. So a line reads `ROLLUP sheet=… by=… person=Ada claimed=10.00 due-total=1.00`. A person with no rate shows `due-total=n/a`, and those people are left out of the sheet's due-total.

**Code changes (server only, no front-end or schema change):**
- **New `rollup/Rollup.java`:** takes the before and after snapshots, compares them and writes the lines. Each service now runs its change through it.
- **New `claim/Dues.java`:** the due-figure and due-total calculations moved here out of `ClaimService`. Both the claims and the rollup need them, and keeping them in `ClaimService` would have made the two services depend on each other. `StatementService` now uses `Dues` too.
- **Lock before measuring:** when an action locks the claim or person (status changes, statements), the lock is taken first and the "before" figures are read after it. Otherwise a stale copy could undermine the existing protection against two users acting on the same record at once.
- **Sheet today:** `SheetService` gets the rollup with `@Lazy`, because the rollup itself reads the sheet's today through `SheetService`.
